articles.title: [Editorial] COPD as a life-course disorder: possibilities and practicalities
articles.author: The Lancet
articles.summary: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is predicted to affect an estimated 600 million people worldwide by 2050, an increase of 23% compared with 2020.

articles.title: [Comment] Izalontamab brengitecan in metastatic breast cancer: is innovation all innovative?
articles.author: Elisabeth G E de Vries, Madeline Pe, Dario Trapani
articles.summary: Approximately two-thirds of patients with breast cancer have hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2–) disease, for which chemotherapy is generally used in the metastatic setting after endocrine-based treatment options, including targeted agents, have been unsuccessful.

articles.title: STAT+: The grueling struggle to find a primary care doctor in the ‘medical capital’ of America
articles.author: Marin Wolf, Jonathan Saltzman,and and Scooty Nickerson — Boston Globe
articles.summary: Boston is supposed to be the medical capital of America. Yet many don’t have primary care access, hurting their ability to get treatments, screenings, and medical advice.

articles.title: Integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance for high-resolution tracking of measles virus evolution and transmission
articles.author: Mukhlid Yousif
articles.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04754-3 Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analyses of wastewater and surveillance samples during the 2024−2025 measles outbreak in South Africa reveal previously undetected inter-provincial spread and transmission links, suggesting that wastewater-integrated whole-genome surveillance can improve measles monitoring and control…

articles.title: Performance of intracortical microelectrode arrays in people with implanted brain–computer interfaces over a 20-year period
articles.author: Shaomin Zhang
articles.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04530-3 Utah arrays recorded stable spiking activity for up to 7.3 years, with modest signal decline on average and sustained movement decoding in the majority of arrays analyzed, demonstrating the long-term feasibility of intracortical brain–computer interfaces.

articles.title: Why Medicare’s 2027 physician pay changes worry some specialists
articles.author: O. Rose Broderick
articles.summary: Cuts to Medicare physician payment rates for certain same-day services could impact some specialists more than others.

articles.title: Pre-eclampsia: Time to focus on delivery rather than discovery
articles.author: Andrew H. Shennan
articles.summary: by Alice Beardmore-Gray, Catherine A. Cluver, Andrew H. Shennan Efforts to reduce maternal mortality have stagnated in the past 5 years and pre-eclampsia remains a leading cause of death.

articles.title: A step towards modelling amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in primates
articles.author: albert-c.ludolph@uni-ulm.de (Liubov Novikova)
articles.summary: A new primate model offers a promising first step towards reproducing the spread of ALS pathology across synapses, although important differences from the stereotyped patterns observed in human disease remain to be addressed.

articles.title: Common supplements rival antibiotics in treating severe gum disease
articles.summary: A combination of omega-3 and low-dose aspirin produced results comparable to antibiotics when used alongside standard treatment for severe gum disease, with benefits persisting long after supplementation ended. The surprising discovery could offer an alternative for some patients while reducing reliance on antibiotics.

articles.title: Loneliness is making us sick, but we may be treating it all wrong
articles.summary: Loneliness can be surprisingly deadly, with previous research linking it to a roughly 30% increase in the risk of premature death. However, a new study warns that treating loneliness as a medical condition could distract from its deeper social causes.

articles.title: Too much of this common nutrient could be accelerating blood vessel aging
articles.summary: Researchers have uncovered a kidney protein that may hold an important key to vascular aging and longevity. The protein helps prevent excess phosphate from accumulating in the blood and gradually turning flexible blood vessels rigid.

articles.title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2I/R9
articles.author: FDA
articles.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved the first medicine for treating limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9), a rare inherited muscle disease, for adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg.

articles.title: FDA Approves First New Hormone Therapy for Early-Stage Breast Cancer in More Than 20 Years
articles.author: FDA
articles.summary: The FDA today approved Wilserdly (giredestrant), used alone after surgery in adults with estrogen receptor–positive, HER2-negative breast cancer — the most common subtype of the disease.

articles.title: Bayer becomes latest Big Pharma to head to Hansoh in $3.3B deal for phase 1 ADC
articles.author: James Waldron
articles.summary: Bayer has become the latest drug giant to turn to Hansoh Pharma for its antibody-drug conjugate expertise.

articles.title: Schrödinger signs €22M biologics collab with sequencing automation outfit Enpicom
articles.author: Michael Gibney
articles.summary: Computational discovery biotech Schrödinger has finalized a collaboration with sequencing automation company Enpicom in an all-cash deal worth €22 million.

articles.title: Mother and three children undergo life-saving heart surgeries within months
articles.summary: Annette Wagner and three of her six children share a bond unlike most families: matching six-inch scars from open-heart surgery.

articles.title: Why breast augmentation looks so different in Brazil and the US
articles.summary: Researchers compare breast surgery practices in Brazil and the US, from implant size and surface to fat grafting, muscle slings and mesh reinforcement.

articles.title: New hormone therapy cuts early breast cancer recurrence risk
articles.summary: A new type of hormone therapy significantly reduced the risk of invasive breast cancer recurrence or death in patients with early-stage, hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer compared with standard treatments, according to findings from a large international phase 3 clinical trial co-led by investigators…

articles.title: Study supports shorter pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor follow-up
articles.summary: Five years of follow-up surveillance—rather than the standard 10—may be adequate for some patients who have had surgery to remove pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, according to a new study led by Cedars-Sinai Health Sciences University investigators.

articles.title: Custom MRI tool could show within weeks if pancreatic cancer treatment is working
articles.summary: About 60% of people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer don't qualify for surgery because their disease is too advanced.

articles.title: Continuing advanced therapies before elective Crohn's surgery may reduce serious complications
articles.summary: Patients with Crohn's disease who continue advanced therapies, including biologics and small-molecule drugs, in the months before elective colorectal surgery may have a lower risk of two postoperative complications: anastomotic leak and organ space surgical site infection, according to a study published in the Journal…

articles.author: Johannes F. Fahrmann

articles.title: Autism symptom severity linked to gastrointestinal problems in children
articles.summary: Researchers at UTHealth Houston have confirmed that children with autism spectrum disorder who experience greater challenges with social awareness and communication may also be more likely to have severe gastrointestinal symptoms.

articles.author: Arkadeep Dhali, Saikat Mandal, Dushyant Singh Dahiya, Guruprasad Aithal
articles.summary: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is an established complication of cystic fibrosis (CF), occurring predominantly in individuals with preserved or partially preserved pancreatic function.

articles.author: Liu, Y., Wang, L.
articles.summary: Gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis (GCPM) remains a formidable clinical challenge, characterised by poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options.

articles.title: Gut feeling: extracellular vesicles dictate livers susceptibility to colorectal cancer metastasis
articles.author: Fiori, M. E.
articles.summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major global health issue, ranking as the third most common tumour and the second leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide.1 Distant metastasis is the primary cause of fatality for patients with cancer.

articles.summary: Researchers engineered a protein system capable of restoring normal chromosome connections in aging mouse eggs, raising hopes of one day improving IVF outcomes

articles.title: New WHO technical package to help countries improve health data for COVID-19 response and beyond
articles.summary: Today, as part of its commitment to strengthening health information systems and improving health[1], especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, WHO announced a new approach to improving access to life-saving data: the SCORE for Health Data Technical Package.

articles.title: COVID-19 disrupting mental health services in most countries, WHO survey
articles.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted or halted critical mental health services in 93% of countries worldwide while the demand for mental health is increasing, according to a new WHO survey.

articles.title: Why government is slow — and how to fix it | Li Hongyi
articles.summary: Government is slow at solving problems — and technologist Li Hongyi wants to fix that. In a quick talk, he introduces his experimental team in the Singaporean government, which visits schools, hospitals, fire stations and communities with one goal: to find problems and prototype solutions.

articles.title: Sunday Pick: How to challenge your self-limiting beliefs with Shawn Achor | from ReThinking with Adam Grant
articles.summary: Your beliefs about yourself and the world have a big impact on your mental health, relationships, and success.

articles.summary: Health officials are urging those at risk of getting flu to get vaccinated as soon as possible.

articles.title: Hospitals in England brace for flu spike with admissions highest for time of year since pre-Covid
articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.summary: NHS chief says hospital bosses should consider asking staff and visitors to wear masks as winter pressures build Hospitals are bracing for a “horrible spike” in flu in the coming days as winter starts to bite, the head of the NHS in England has said.

articles.author: Justin Bergman, International Affairs Editor, The Conversation
articles.summary: The trial of former president of the Philippines, Rodrigo Duterte, comes at a precarious moment for the International Criminal Court, as the US ramps up its efforts to undermine the institution.

articles.author: Markian Hawryluk
articles.summary: Any discussion of a universal health plan in the U.S. always comes with concerns about massive costs. The challenge for proponents is to explain to voters that Americans already spend more than $5 trillion on healthcare each year.
